I confirmed with the account team today that Harbor Health's contract requires downloadable access to its registry artifacts for 730 days after registry retirement. This was found during a customer-renewal review and hasn't been attached to the platform ticket yet. A July 31 hard shutdown of read access would violate Harbor Health's contractual artifact access rights, so the retirement plan needs to account for extended downloadable access for that customer before Riley approves.
transcript.speaker: A3

commitments.detail: Update the retirement ticket to include read-only compatibility access for the six active release branches (payments-v3, mobile-android-2025.06, mobile-ios-2025.06, desktop-4.8, analytics-2.3, edge-agent-1.9) until their releases complete, instead of a July 31 hard read shutdown.

Attach Harbor Health's 730-day contractual artifact access requirement to the platform ticket and ensure extended downloadable read access for Harbor Health artifacts is provisioned before legacy write access is shut off.
Open the privacy finding and update the retirement plan to specify bearer-token fragment redaction and 14-day log retention, replacing the 90-day retention in the draft plan.

Write access will be shut off on July 31 as planned. Read access will remain available via allowlist for the six flagged release branches until release completion and for Harbor Health artifacts for 730 days post-retirement. Registry logs will have token fragments redacted and be purged after 14 days.
